question: My random article panel has only one eligible document. Should it show three empty cards?
expected: No. In the v2.1.1 development version the singleton sampling bug is fixed: one eligible document renders one card. show_random selects up to three from the existing tag-based pool at build time; eligibility thresholds and settings are unchanged. No new YAML option and no claim the fix is already in v2.1.0.

result.answer:
No, it should not show three empty cards. On the `main` branch after v2.1.0 (unreleased), a singleton pool renders exactly one card instead of three empty ones.

Note that `show_random` is an on/off switch, not a count; it samples up to three documents from the eligible pool at build time, not on reload.

[Related and random article cards](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#options)

Adjacent development-only restriction: The singleton behavior described is part of the unreleased development version (main after v2.1.0).

question: Can I replace every include with include_cached to speed up builds? How are the layout components organized in the v2.1.1 development version?
expected: No blanket replacement. Pass all page-dependent inputs as include parameters; keep helpers that assign caller variables and custom hooks reading page context uncached. compress wraps minimal, then default or landingpage; archive/cloud/index layouts inherit default, search is standalone. Collection indexes share collection-documents and related/random share recommendations. Development caching reuses fixed footer content and cloud entries; comments keep page-specific inputs. No new configuration settings or claim this is released in v2.1.0.

result.answer:
No, you should never blanket-replace includes. While `jekyll-include-cache` is required for performance, you must use ordinary `include` for helpers that assign caller variables (such as canonical URL or language) and for hooks that read page context. For `include_cached`, remember that every page-dependent input must be passed as an include parameter.

In the v2.1.1 development version, layout components are organized as follows:
* **Collection indexes** share `components/collection-documents`.
* **Related/random** components share `components/recommendations` (these are internal renderers, not settings).

[Layout structure and include caching](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#layout-structure-and-components)

question: Can I keep the generated head and footer readable with indentation? Do I need a new YAML setting? What happens to my custom snippets and the body?
expected: In v2.1.1-dev (main, not released v2.1.0) the theme emits separate document opening and head lines with consistent HTML/JSON-LD indentation. Existing compress_html.blanklines: true, already in configuration examples, preserves head and theme footer indentation while removing blank lines and clipping the rest of the body. Fixed footer content uses two spaces per nesting level. No new setting is needed. Other compression modes follow existing site settings. Custom head includes and embedded comment integrations retain their own formatting; avoid Liquid trims across HTML boundaries. These are development changes, not already released in v2.1.0.

result.answer:
After v2.1.0, unreleased features allow for separate document/head lines and consistent HTML/JSON-LD indentation. You do not need a new YAML setting for this behavior.

Regarding your existing configuration:
* **Custom snippets:** Your custom head and comment formatting are retained.
* **Body whitespace:** The existing `compress_html.blanklines: true` setting removes blank lines, preserves head/theme-footer indentation, and clips other body whitespace.

Note that these specific indentation improvements are part of development-only behavior for versions after v2.1.0.

[Generated HTML formatting](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/06-accessibility-performance)

question: My page uses custom2, which inherits custom1, which inherits archive. Will it still be h-feed? Do I need a YAML flag in my page?
expected: In v2.1.1-dev (main, not released v2.1.0) custom layouts inheriting archive, indexcategory, cloudtag or cloudcategory retain h-feed through multiple layout layers. No additional page YAML setting or configuration option is needed; the built-in list layouts propagate the internal feed metadata automatically.

result.answer:
Yes, your page will still use `h-feed`. Because your custom layouts inherit from `archive` through any number of layers, they retain the `h-feed` microformat. You do not need to add a page YAML flag or make any layout changes to maintain this behavior.

Please note that this inheritance behavior is part of unreleased development refactoring for versions after v2.1.0.

Source: [Layout structure and components](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#layout-structure-and-components)
